name: upgrade-never-clobbers
body: Upgrade never overwrites author content. It writes only kalide-owned scaffold files (requirements.requirement.upgrade-refresh-owned-scaffold) and only when the target file is byte-identical to a known released kalide version of that same file — or, for the two full guides only, when `AGENTS_KALIDE.md` is absent — plus the one deliberate exception that brings the `AGENTS.md` pointer to the reference scheme: when an `AGENTS.md` is absent it is created carrying the reference; when it is byte-identical to a known released full guide it is migrated (replaced by the short reference file, with `AGENTS_KALIDE.md` written); when it is author content without the reference string the reference line is appended and its other bytes are preserved; and when it already carries the string it is left byte-for-byte untouched. Appending the reference line to a present author `AGENTS.md` is the one permitted modification of that file (agent-guide-reference). A file whose bytes match no known released version is treated as author content and left byte-for-byte untouched, and a file already byte-identical to the running kalide's version of that same file is already current — a no-op, left as-is and not re-written. Author content — slide files and their frontmatter, author templates/sections/themes/media, `kalide.yaml` author keys, a library's templates — is never a write candidate. Every skipped, every appended/migrated and every refreshed path is reported. There is no `--force` flag and no partial overwrite.
